classification.note: The repository is a Ghidra-export-to-assembler reconstruction tool, not a completed game port.

target_cpu.note: compile.sh explicitly invokes vasmm68k_mot -m68000 for the generated AM2_CPU.s output.

build.note: A compile command is present, but upstream documents no successful rebuild, comparison, or byte-identity result.

runtime_profiles.note: README and compile script give no minimum host or Amiga runtime requirements.

ai.note: No explicit AI use appears in the reviewed README, compile script, or source tree.

relationships.note: The README directly identifies Ambermoon AM2_CPU/AM2_BLIT as the input relationship.

next_actions: Verify a successful AM2_CPU/AM2_BLIT assembly and compare its output with the original binaries.

identity.note: README identifies AmiXcom 0.9.14 as the classic-Amiga OpenXcom port covering UFO and TFTD rulesets.

classification.note: It remains a native Amiga port of an open-source reimplementation, not a newly reverse-engineered X-COM binary.

target_cpu.note: README and build flags explicitly require 68020+ and compile with -mcpu=68020: https://github.com/angree/AmiXcom/blob/main/README.md

build.note: 0.9.14 release documentation says the whole game runs and records hours of testing while explicitly stopping short of end-to-end completion; the release adds AdLib conversion and AmiXcomPrefs.

runtime_profiles.note: Captured only the explicit AGA 68020+, Kickstart 3.0+, no-FPU and ~50 MB Fast-RAM floor; the less-tested RTG build has no inferred minimum.

ai.note: README explicitly states the port was made with Claude Code and current commits carry Claude co-author/session evidence.

relationships.note: README explicitly identifies OpenXcom as upstream and the author's OpenTTD 68k port as the source of the platform layer.
